scope.description: Re-run of the four-case probe with a transport that cannot jam behind a parked destination, so the node-local park, the cluster-level stall and the default-capacity bound are all measured under the same delivery semantics.
assumptions: in-process 3-node cluster, majority quorum, error-free memory storage
event consumption is the only variable between the park cases and the control
writes are paced so consecutive decided-index changes are observed in separate ticks
excluded: deployments whose clients always drain events
any latency claim about how long a real cluster needs to reach the bound

basis.prefix: Same harness as the executed revision, with the transport replaced as described. Cases: (1) `unconsumed_event_stream_stops_actor_loop` - 3 nodes, none consuming events, event_capacity 64, paced 4ms proposals until a node's actor stops answering, asserting the parked node's channel is full and live and that its append_notify endpoint is withheld (emits unconsumed_event_bound_reached, actor_parked, append_notify_endpoint_withheld); (2) `drained_event_stream_keeps_actor_loop_running` - the control with every event stream drained (emits control_actors_responsive, control_append_notify); (3) `parked_majority_stops_the_cluster_deciding` - only node 1 consumes events, event_capacity 8, two nodes park and the healthy node's write cannot be decided (emits parked_majority_cluster); (4) `default_capacity_event_bound_stops_actor_loop` - only node 1 consumes events with `RuntimeConfig::default()` left unchanged (event_capacity 1024), 4000 proposals paced at 1ms so the two unread nodes keep observing transitions until they reach the bound, then the healthy node's decided index must be unchanged and its write must not complete (emits default_capacity_parked_cluster). All four cases run in one execution.

before.description: Bound measurement at the shipped default event capacity: does an unconsumed event stream park nodes and stall the cluster when the capacity is left at 1024?
assumptions: in-process 3-node cluster, majority quorum, in-process transport under harness control
only node 1 consumes its event stream; nodes 2 and 3 leave the handle's receiver unread
writes are paced at one per millisecond so consecutive decided-index changes are observed in separate ticks
excluded: deployments whose clients always drain events
any latency claim about how long a real cluster needs to reach 1024 transitions

after.description: Re-run of the four-case probe with a transport that cannot jam behind a parked destination, so the node-local park, the cluster-level stall and the default-capacity bound are all measured under the same delivery semantics.
assumptions: in-process 3-node cluster, majority quorum, error-free memory storage

writes are paced so consecutive decided-index changes are observed in separate ticks
excluded: deployments whose clients always drain events

prefix.before: Same in-process 3-node cluster and actor setup as the executed revision (real OmniPaxos instances over MemoryStorage warmed by omnipaxos_runtime actors spawned with spawn_actor and a harness-local tokio-backed AsyncRuntime impl; one delivery task per node forwards outgoing messages to the receiver's handle_incoming). The new case drains events only on node 1 and leaves the default capacity in place (RuntimeConfig::default().event_capacity = 1024), then paces ordinary writes from the elected leader (one proposal per millisecond, 4000 proposals) so that the two unread nodes keep observing transitions until they reach the bound; it waits up to 90s for both to stop answering commands, then measures whether the healthy node 1 can still decide: it emits CA_EVENT default_capacity_parked_cluster {event_capacity,nodes_parked,decided_before,decided_after,append_notify_timeout_reached} and asserts that both unread nodes parked, that node 1 stayed responsive, that its decided index was unchanged across the attempt, and that at least 1024 transitions had been observed before the two nodes parked (so the bound really was the default rather than a smaller configured one).
prefix.after: Same harness as the executed revision, with the transport replaced as described. Cases: (1) `unconsumed_event_stream_stops_actor_loop` - 3 nodes, none consuming events, event_capacity 64, paced 4ms proposals until a node's actor stops answering, asserting the parked node's channel is full and live and that its append_notify endpoint is withheld (emits unconsumed_event_bound_reached, actor_parked, append_notify_endpoint_withheld); (2) `drained_event_stream_keeps_actor_loop_running` - the control with every event stream drained (emits control_actors_responsive, control_append_notify); (3) `parked_majority_stops_the_cluster_deciding` - only node 1 consumes events, event_capacity 8, two nodes park and the healthy node's write cannot be decided (emits parked_majority_cluster); (4) `default_capacity_event_bound_stops_actor_loop` - only node 1 consumes events with `RuntimeConfig::default()` left unchanged (event_capacity 1024), 4000 proposals paced at 1ms so the two unread nodes keep observing transitions until they reach the bound, then the healthy node's decided index must be unchanged and its write must not complete (emits default_capacity_parked_cluster). All four cases run in one execution.

revision_reason: Transport correction only; the four cases, their assertions and their parameters are unchanged. The previous run's new case failed with its own operands showing the artefact: event `default_capacity_parked_cluster` recorded nodes_parked 1, decided_before 1030 = decided_after 1030, although only one node had parked, so a quorum (the healthy leader plus the other live follower) was still available - progress had stopped because each sender's forwarding task was blocked awaiting delivery into the parked node's full incoming channel, which also stalls that sender's unrelated traffic. Delivery is now per destination: senders only push into the destination's queue and one task per destination awaits handle_incoming, so a parked destination accumulates messages in its own queue and cannot block anyone else. The same correction removes that confound from the cluster-level case in the same harness. Locally all four cases pass with the corrected transport (11.5s), with the default-capacity case reporting event_capacity 1024, nodes_parked 2, decided_before = decided_after = 1119 and append_notify_timeout_reached true.
